stem.en: Why do periods stop during pregnancy?

text.en: Hormones keep the lining, and no eggs are released.

feedback.en: Correct. The lining is in use, so it is not shed.

text.en: The ovaries run out of eggs once one egg is fertilised.

feedback.en: The ovaries still hold many eggs. They are simply not released in pregnancy.

text.en: The zygote uses up all the blood, so none is left to shed.

feedback.en: The mother's blood supply continues. The lining stays in place because of hormones.

text.en: A cycle can run for only 28 days, and pregnancy lasts longer.

feedback.en: Cycles vary in length, and that is not why periods stop.

explanation.en: A period is the shedding of the lining. In pregnancy the lining is needed, so hormones keep it in place. No more eggs are released, so the monthly cycle stops.
